places.backstage: Setting: behind a heavy dark-red stage curtain in a hotel ballroom, cables on the floor, a stack of folding chairs, a strip of warm light through a gap in the curtain.
places.corridor: Setting: a narrow hotel service corridor behind a ballroom, steel service carts, fluorescent light, swinging kitchen doors with round windows.
places.stairwell: Setting: a concrete hotel stairwell with a narrow wired-glass window looking into a lit ballroom, cold fluorescent light.

places.catering: Setting: a hotel catering hall, stainless counters, a walk-in fridge door, two white bakery boxes on rolling carts, bright work lights.

places.foyer: Setting: a hotel foyer and coat check at night, a brass coat rack, glass front doors, cold night outside.

places.apartment_day: Setting: the same small apartment kitchen in late afternoon sunlight, a wooden table with two chairs.

places.bakery_kitchen: Setting: the back kitchen of a small family bakery before dawn, steel worktables, deck ovens, sheet pans, flour on everything, a schedule taped to the wall.
places.bakery_front: Setting: the front counter of a small warm family bakery in the morning, bread racks, a glass pastry case, chalkboard menu, little café tables by the window.

scenes.image: Close-up of Megan at a live microphone on the small stage, smiling fondly, spotlight on her.
lines: [fond, polished, as if she's told it a hundred times] I dropped Dad's birthday cake when I was twelve. [pause] He stuck the candles in the part that landed right side up.
sfx: Live microphone hum in a quiet ballroom
scenes.motion: she leans into the microphone, smiling, the spotlight glinting on her earrings

scenes.image: Wide shot of the ballroom: a hundred guests at round tables laughing toward the stage.
sfx: A large party crowd laughing warmly
scenes.motion: guests laugh and lean back in their chairs, glasses raised

scenes.image: At the back of the ballroom, Rachel frozen in the aisle, a white cake box tied with string pressed against her flour-dusted work jacket.
lines: [quiet] At the back of the room, a woman in a flour-dusted work jacket stopped walking. [pause] She was holding the birthday cake.
scenes.motion: Rachel stops dead, the cake box pressed against her chest, the laughter rolling past her

scenes.image: The host stepping up beside the stage with his arm out, grinning.
lines: [big, warm, showman] Frank's daughter, Rachel, everybody!
scenes.motion: the host sweeps his arm toward the woman at the microphone as applause starts

scenes.image: Frank hugging Megan on stage; over her shoulder his eyes have found someone at the back of the room.
lines: [slow] Frank hugged her. [pause] Over her shoulder, he saw his real daughter. [pause] His hand stayed on the stranger's back.
scenes.motion: Frank pulls Megan into a hug, then his eyes lift over her shoulder and lock on someone; his hand stays on her back

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel's face, very still, eyes on the stage.
lines: [just loud enough, very still] Dad. [pause] Who is she?
scenes.motion: the applause dies around her; she doesn't blink

scenes.image: Ben cutting across the aisle with a drink in his hand, smile switched on, waving at a server.
lines: [bright, smiling too wide, to a server] Perfect! The cake's here. [pause] Could you show her to the kitchen?
scenes.motion: Ben strides down the aisle with a drink, smile switching on

scenes.image: Rachel and Ben face to face in the aisle, guests watching from the tables.
lines: [holding the smile, through his teeth] She's with the bakery.
scenes.motion: Ben keeps smiling at the guests while Rachel stares at him

scenes.image: A young server in a black vest taking one step back; a woman at a nearby table turning her chair to watch.
lines: [dry] The server took one step back. [pause] A woman near the aisle turned her chair around.
scenes.motion: the server backs away; a guest swivels her chair to watch

scenes.image: Ben leaning in close to Rachel, voice dropped, eyes on the guests.
lines: [under his breath, charming] Can we do this outside?
[low] Where did she hear that story?
[a light shrug] It's a party. People tell stories.
scenes.motion: Ben leans in close, still smiling for the room

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel, jaw tight, holding the cake box.
lines: [quiet, precise] Dad tells everybody the cake landed on the table. [pause] It landed on the floor. [pause] I told you the real version on Sunday.
scenes.motion: her grip tightens on the cake box

scenes.image: Ben reaching for the cake box; Rachel pulling it back against her chest.
lines: [a tight smile] You're standing in the middle of the aisle.
scenes.motion: Ben reaches for the box and Rachel pulls it back against her chest

scenes.image: Close-up of Ben, smile gone soft, almost pleading.
lines: [soft, as if asking a favor] Dad gets one night.
[very quiet] Then ask him who I am.
scenes.motion: Ben's smile fades into something softer and more dangerous

scenes.image: Megan on stage lowering the microphone, uncertain, looking toward the aisle.
lines: [polish cracking, one note of uncertainty] Do we... need to stop?

scenes.image: Frank taking the microphone from Megan, looking down the room toward his daughter.
lines: [slow] Frank took the microphone. [pause] He looked straight down the aisle at Rachel. [pause] She shifted the cake box onto one arm, ready to lift her hand when he said her name.

scenes.image: Frank handing the microphone back to Megan with a gentle smile.
lines: [gently, warm public voice, to Megan] Go ahead, sweetheart.
sfx: A single person clapping once, then stopping

scenes.image: Rachel in the aisle with her hand half raised, slowly lowering it.
lines: [very quiet] Somebody clapped once. [pause] Then stopped.

scenes.image: Megan setting the microphone down on the stand, pale.
lines: [small] Could I get a glass of water?

scenes.image: The host catching Ben by the sleeve at the edge of the stage, grinning through clenched teeth.
lines: [through his smile] What do you want me to do up here?

scenes.image: Ben looking at an empty rolling cart beside the stage.
lines: [dry] Ben looked at the empty cart beside the stage.

scenes.image: Behind the curtain, Megan pulling a folded page out of her dress pocket while Rachel watches.
lines: [quick, keeping her voice down] They told me it was a reenactment. I asked if you were coming. [pause] He said you'd be watching at home.
[low] What else did they give you?

scenes.image: Megan holding out the folded page.
lines: This goes after the cake. [pause] He told me to look straight into the camera.

scenes.image: Close-up of a printed page: the words FINAL TAKE at the top, one sentence highlighted in yellow underneath.
lines: [reading slowly, each word heavier] "Starting tomorrow... Ben will run the bakery. [pause] This was my decision."

overlay.text: FINAL TAKE — "Starting tomorrow, Ben will run the bakery. This was my decision."

scenes.image: Megan studying Rachel's face; Rachel staring at the page.
lines: [a dry, exhausted breath] I opened the bakery at four this morning. [pause] He texted me to ask where we keep the keys.

scenes.image: Through a gap in the red curtain: the videographer's camera on its tripod turning toward an empty spot beside Frank on stage.
lines: [over the speakers, cheerful] Can we get Rachel back up here? We've got one more thing to film!

scenes.image: Both women turning toward the stage at the same moment, faces lit through the curtain gap.
lines: [a beat, then low] Both women looked toward the stage.

scenes.image: Rachel setting the cake box down on a steel service cart in the corridor.
lines: [matter-of-fact] Rachel set the cake down on a service cart. [pause] Then she walked straight to the camera.

scenes.image: Rachel standing squarely in front of the videographer's lens, controlled.
lines: [controlled, quiet] That page she was about to read? I've never said any of it. [pause] Please stop filming.

scenes.image: The videographer lowering his camera, confused.
lines: [uneasy, helpful] Do you want us to skip the speech and just use the shop footage?

scenes.image: On a small video monitor: Megan behind a bakery counter tying a flour-stained apron, smiling for the camera.
lines: [bright, rehearsed] My dad opened this place before I was born. Pretty much everything I know... I learned right here.

scenes.image: Close-up on the monitor: the flour stain on the apron pocket.
lines: [quiet] Rachel knew that apron. [pause] She knew the flour stain on the pocket. [pause] It was hers.

scenes.image: Rachel staring at the monitor; the videographer beside her.
Memory: the small family bakery at dusk, the CLOSED sign being flipped on the glass door.
lines: [low] On Tuesday, Ben had offered to close for her. [pause] It was the first time he'd offered in three years.

scenes.image: Rachel leaning toward the monitor.
lines: [steady] Can you play what happens next?

scenes.image: On the monitor: Megan turning toward someone off camera, unsure.
lines: [off-camera, casual] Yeah. Next time, stay behind the counter. [pause] I don't want anyone outside getting a good look at you.

scenes.image: The videographer stopping the clip himself, embarrassed.
lines: [embarrassed] He told me she worked there.
[not unkind] You took direction from him. I get it. [pause] Who has the footage?
I sent him the previews this morning. [pause] The originals are with me.

scenes.image: Rachel in the concrete stairwell, phone to her ear.
lines: [machinery behind her, dry] If this is about the lemon filling, I put it on the bottom shelf.
sfx: Industrial mixer and kitchen machinery over a phone line

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel, one hand on the stair rail.
lines: [low] Tuesday night. Did you see anybody behind my counter?

scenes.image: Nina in the bakery kitchen with the phone wedged against her shoulder, flour on her arms.
lines: [dry] Ben sent me home early. Said he was taking pictures of the ovens for insurance. [pause] Why?
[very quiet] Did he ask you to leave my apron out?

scenes.image: Nina stopping, wiping her hands on a towel.
lines: [dry, a little amused] He asked which one you wear on camera. [pause] I told him you wear the same one until I physically take it off you.

scenes.image: Rachel pressing her knuckles to her mouth, almost laughing, eyes wet.
lines: [quiet] Rachel almost laughed. [pause] Nina heard her breathing change.

scenes.image: Rachel looking down the stairwell.
lines: [flat] Got a new one an hour ago. Same start time. [pause] Different name at the top.
Who does it say to call if something goes wrong?
[dry] Ben. [pause] I called him twice about the delivery. He hasn't picked up.

scenes.image: Through the wired-glass stairwell window: Ben in the ballroom showing a guest his phone; the screen lights up with an incoming call and he flips it face down.
lines: [slow] Through the stairwell window, Rachel watched Ben show a guest something on his phone. [pause] A call lit up the screen. [pause] He turned it face down.

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel, eyes hard.
lines: [quiet, decided] Keep that schedule. [pause] And send me a picture before he changes it.

scenes.image: Megan standing beside the cake cart with her coat over one arm, ready to leave.
lines: [awkward, plain voice] I was going to leave your page with the cake.
[tired] It's his page. You can keep it.

scenes.image: Megan turning to go; Rachel stopping her with a question.
lines: [a sudden thought, quiet] Who told you how I wear the towel?

scenes.image: Megan pausing, embarrassed.
lines: [honest] Ben showed me a video. You were making something with your dad. [pause] You kept wiping your hands every time he asked you a question.
[a faint, sad smile] He was trying to get me to look up for the camera.

scenes.image: Megan miming a little downward glance and smile.
lines: Ben wanted me to copy that thing you do before you answer. [pause] Where you look down and... kind of smile to yourself.

scenes.image: Rachel looking down with a tiny private smile, then catching herself.
lines: [soft] Rachel looked down. [pause] She caught herself.

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel, eyes glistening.
lines: [quiet, it costs her] I made that video for Dad. [pause] He was supposed to watch it after the party.

scenes.image: Megan glancing toward the ballroom doors as the host's voice calls the family up.
lines: [distant, over the speakers] Could we get Frank and the family up here for a photo?
[a breath] I can tell the camera guy what they hired me for.
[looking at the closed doors] Would you tell the people in there?

scenes.image: Megan sliding her coat off her arm and laying it over the cart handle.
lines: [slow] Megan looked toward the ballroom. [pause] Then she slid her coat off her arm.
[plain, steady] If you're in there with me.

scenes.image: Mara stepping into the corridor with two glasses of water, handing one over.
lines: [friendly, getting right to it] I thought I saw you come in. [pause] Can we talk about tomorrow?
[careful] If Ben told you the tasting's canceled... it isn't.

scenes.image: Mara and Rachel close together in the corridor.
lines: [exact] He told me it was going ahead. [pause] He said you asked him to take over.
Monday. I asked to speak to you. [pause] He said you were too upset. [pause] So I called your dad.

scenes.image: Through the glass of the ballroom door: Frank making room for Ben in the family photo, an empty spot on his other side.
lines: [slow] Through the glass, Frank made room for Ben in the family photo. [pause] On his other side, there was an empty spot.

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel, holding very still.
lines: [almost no voice] What did Dad say?
[gently] "Give Ben a chance." [pause] I thought he meant a chance to run the meeting. [pause] Then I got this.

scenes.image: Close-up of Mara's phone: an email from Frank with a speech attached.
Rachel reading her phone, the glow on her face.
lines: [low] Her phone buzzed a moment later. [pause] On Frank's copy, there was a note at the bottom. [pause] It wasn't on Megan's.

scenes.image: Close-up of a phone screen with a typed note at the bottom of a speech.
lines: [almost too quiet to hear] "Do this after the cake. [pause] She'll have gone home by then."

overlay.text: "Do this after the cake. She'll have gone home by then."

scenes.image: Rachel lifting the cake box off the cart; Megan beside her.
lines: [steady, quiet] I want to hear my dad say it.

scenes.image: Aunt Linda beaming from the front row, patting an empty chair.
lines: [light] The photographer was calling for everyone to move in a little.
[fond, oblivious] There she is! I saved you a chair.

scenes.image: Rachel setting the cake box on the edge of the stage; Frank's eyes on the box.
lines: [warm public voice] You made the one with lemon.

scenes.image: The photographer's camera raised; Rachel looking only at her father.
lines: [quiet, direct] Did you email Mara on Monday?
[light, deflecting] Honey, she's here as a guest.
[quieter] She was a guest when you told her I quit?

scenes.image: Ben sliding between his father and the center of the room, hand up to the photographer.
lines: [smooth, to the photographer] Can you give us one minute? [pause] Dad needs to sit down.

scenes.image: Frank standing still, not sitting.
lines: [dry] The photographer lowered the camera. [pause] Frank made no move to sit.

scenes.image: Aunt Linda's smile falling.
lines: [confused, hurt] Why would you tell somebody Rachel quit?
[smooth] She hasn't quit. We're changing a few things. Dad wanted to tell you himself.

scenes.image: Frank glancing at the camera, which now points at the floor.
lines: [low, his small private voice] Come out here with me.

scenes.image: Close-up of Frank avoiding his daughter's eyes.
lines: [intimate, slow] Rachel had watched her father tell customers they'd lost an order. Lost a deposit. Lost the power on Christmas Eve. [pause] He always looked them in the eye. [pause] He still hadn't looked at her... since he'd put his arm around that woman.

scenes.image: The tiny venue office: Frank leaving the door open an inch, Rachel pushing it shut behind them.
lines: [quiet] The office was barely big enough for three chairs. [pause] Frank left the door open an inch. [pause] Rachel closed it.
sfx: A door clicking shut in a small room

scenes.image: Frank sitting heavily, weary.
lines: [weary, trying for tender] Your brother came to me in September. [pause] He said he wanted to come home.
[even] I offered him the Tuesday close.

scenes.image: Father and daughter facing each other across the small desk.
lines: [quiet] He took it once. [pause] You just saw what he did with it.
[a small shrug] He's good with people. You've always known that.

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel.
lines: [controlled] The woman he hired thought she was here to tell a funny story about me.
[defensive] I was told she knew what the whole thing was for.
[quieter] What did you think the whole thing was for?

scenes.image: Frank rubbing the pale strip on his wrist where his watch usually sits.
lines: [slow, half to himself] I wanted people to keep coming in Monday morning. Same bread. Same girls behind the counter. [pause] They hear I'm retiring and they start to worry. [pause] I wanted them to see we'd figured it out. [pause] As a family.

scenes.image: Rachel waiting, arms folded.
lines: [very quiet] Which part did we figure out together?

scenes.image: Frank looking at the door instead of his daughter.
lines: [a pause that costs him, then] You could have asked me for the business years ago.
[quietly] I did. [pause] You said we'd talk when you retired.

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel, a silence hanging.
lines: [almost gentle] We're at your retirement party, Dad.
sfx: Faint muffled party music through a wall

scenes.image: Ben letting himself into the office, all business.
lines: [brisk, charming] Mara's still here. [pause] We need to give her one story.

scenes.image: Ben leaning on the desk.
lines: [easy] The real one is she wants a bigger order than you wanted to take. [pause] I said yes.
[precise] She wanted to run a tasting. We hadn't agreed to the order.

scenes.image: Ben and Rachel facing off in the cramped room.
lines: [a flash of irritation] That's because every time she asked what we could do, you told her what could go wrong.
[quiet] I told her we had one oven that could hold temperature.

scenes.image: Frank looking up, surprised.
lines: [to Ben, confused] I thought the second one was fixed.
[tired] It was quoted. [pause] I sent you the quote twice.

scenes.image: Ben spreading his hands with a laugh.
lines: [a short laugh, charming again] Listen to us. We're at Dad's party arguing over an oven. [pause] This is exactly why I said I'd handle the business side.
[very quiet] How many stores did you promise?

scenes.image: Close-up of Ben taking a drink, then setting the glass down deliberately.
lines: [slow] Ben took a drink. [pause] He set the glass down very carefully.
sfx: A glass set down on a wooden desk

scenes.image: Frank turning to look at his son for the first time.
lines: [a shrug] Two was last week. She got excited.

scenes.image: Rachel, arms crossed, eyes narrowed.
lines: [quiet, exact] She saw samples for two stores. [pause] Did you tell her who'd be making the six-store order?
[as if it's obvious] I told her we had a team.

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel's phone on the desk: a photo of a new staff schedule and six handwritten sample labels laid out in a row.
lines: [low] Rachel's phone lit up. Nina had sent the new schedule. [pause] And a photo of six labels, laid out in a row.

overlay.text: New schedule + the labels he left out. 6 of them.

scenes.image: Rachel sliding the phone between her father and brother.
lines: [quiet] Is there supposed to be a tray for each of those?

scenes.image: Close-up of Rachel.
lines: [very even] On which day were you going to tell us to make six trays?

scenes.image: Ben waving a hand.
lines: [impatient] They don't have to be the exact same thing we'd ship. [pause] Let somebody make it look good for the meeting.
[flat] You invited a buyer to a tasting. [pause] She'll taste it.

scenes.image: Frank turning to Ben, uneasy.
lines: [uneasy] Ben, just tell her we need more time.
[sharp] You tell her. You're the one she trusts.

scenes.image: Frank's hand moving toward his jacket pocket, then stopping.
lines: [quiet] Frank's hand moved toward his jacket pocket. [pause] Then it stopped.

scenes.image: Ben leaning close to Rachel, voice dropping, persuasive.
lines: [dropping his voice, generous] You can still come in tomorrow. [pause] If that's what you're worried about.

scenes.image: Ben looking at Frank; Frank looking down at the schedule on the phone.
lines: [slow] Ben looked at Frank. [pause] Frank looked down at the schedule.

scenes.image: Memory: the family bakery before dawn, one light on in the back, a coffee mug steaming on the counter.
lines: [intimate, slow] Every morning Frank arrived, there was coffee in his mug and bread on the rack. [pause] Sometimes he'd tell a customer he still opened the place himself. [pause] Rachel used to think it was a joke.
[quiet] Standing between the two men, she realized... neither of them knew when the first person came through the door.

scenes.image: Rachel slipping out into the backstage area, stopping at the curtain because she hears her father's voice.
lines: [low] The host needed Ben for his next cue. Rachel slipped out. [pause] From behind the curtain, she heard her father talking to Megan.

scenes.image: Frank and Megan behind the curtain, Frank pointing at the page in her hand.
lines: [careful, almost kind] At the end, say, "I decided."
[plain] My page says, "This was my decision."

scenes.image: Close-up of Frank, a little impatient.
lines: [soft] Yes. Either way. [pause] Ben's copy says, "We decided." I don't want that in there.
[quiet, pointed] What if she never decided?

scenes.image: Rachel standing behind the curtain, the red fabric almost brushing her face.
lines: [very quiet] Silence. [pause] Rachel stood so close to the curtain the fabric almost brushed her face.

scenes.image: Frank sighing at Megan.
lines: [tired] I'm asking you to get us through the evening.
[steady] I think you should ask her.

scenes.image: Frank's irritation showing.
lines: [irritation breaking through] I know how that conversation would go. [pause] I've been her father for thirty-eight years.
